subject: evs
prompt_en: Look at a toy in a mirror and at its shadow on the wall. Give two differences.
prompt_hi: Ek khilone ko sheeshe mein dekho aur deewar pe uski parchhai dekho. Do farak batao.
answer: The mirror shows the toy's colours and details; the shadow is just a dark outline with no colour or details. The mirror image comes from light bouncing back; the shadow is where light is blocked.

subject: evs
prompt_en: At 5 pm the Sun is in the west. Which way does the shadow of a lamp post point?
prompt_hi: Shaam 5 baje Sooraj paschim mein hai. Bijli ke khambhe ki parchhai kis taraf padegi?
answer: East.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In a village, people sit in a tree's shade. At noon the shade is right under the tree, but by evening it has moved and grown. Why does the shady spot move during the day?
prompt_hi: Gaon mein log ped ki chhaaya mein baithte hain. Dopahar mein chhaaya theek ped ke neeche hoti hai, par shaam tak woh khisak ke lambi ho jaati hai. Din bhar chhaaya kyon khisakti hai?
answer: The Sun's place in the sky changes as the Earth turns, so the tree's shadow changes direction and length: it moves to the side away from the Sun and gets longer as the Sun gets lower.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In this picture the Sun is low on the left side of a house. Point to where the house's shadow will be, and say whether it is long or short.
prompt_hi: Is picture mein Sooraj ghar ke left side mein neeche hai. Batao ghar ki parchhai kahan hogi, aur lambi hogi ya chhoti?
answer: On the right side of the house, and long, because the Sun is low.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Every day the Sun walks across the sky from east to west, going around the Earth.' What is a better explanation?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Roz Sooraj aasmaan mein poorab se paschim tak chalta hai, Dharti ke chakkar lagaate hue.' Isse behtar explanation kya hai?
answer: The Earth spins once a day, so the Sun only seems to move across our sky.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why his shadow is long in the morning, short at lunchtime and long again in the evening.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki uski parchhai subah lambi, dopahar mein chhoti, aur shaam ko phir lambi kyon hoti hai.
answer: In the morning and evening the Sun is low, so the shadow is long; at noon the Sun is high, so it is short; the shadow is always opposite the Sun, and the Sun's position changes because the Earth spins.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: what is a shadow, in one line?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek line mein batao, parchhai kya hoti hai?
answer: A dark area formed where an object blocks light.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What do we call the night when we see the full round Moon, and the night when we can't see the Moon at all?
prompt_hi: Jis raat poora gol chaand dikhta hai use kya kehte hain, aur jis raat chaand bilkul nahi dikhta use kya?
answer: Full Moon: Purnima. No Moon visible: Amavasya (new moon).

subject: evs
prompt_en: About how many days is it from one Purnima to the next Purnima?
prompt_hi: Ek Purnima se agli Purnima tak lagbhag kitne din hote hain?
answer: About 29 to 30 days, about a month.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Tonight is Purnima. Predict: about one week from now, will the Moon look more lit, the same, or less lit?
prompt_hi: Aaj Purnima hai. Guess karo: lagbhag ek hafte baad chaand zyada roshan dikhega, waisa hi, ya kam?
answer: Less lit: about half of it (a half-moon), shrinking toward Amavasya.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In a dark room, shine a torch on a white ball from one side. Walk slowly around the ball. Predict: will the lit part look the same from everywhere?
prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein ek taraf se torch se safed ball pe roshni daalo. Ball ke chaaron taraf dheere-dheere ghoomo. Guess karo: kya roshan hissa har jagah se ek jaisa dikhega?
answer: No: from some spots you see it fully lit, from others half-lit or as a thin sliver, and from one spot almost dark, like the Moon's phases. The ball itself never changes.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A few days after Amavasya you see a thin crescent Moon. Predict: over the next week, will it get thicker or thinner?
prompt_hi: Amavasya ke kuch din baad tumhe patla sa chaand dikhta hai. Guess karo: agle hafte woh mota hoga ya aur patla?
answer: Thicker: the lit part grows toward Purnima.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why does the Moon seem to change shape over a month?
prompt_hi: Mahine bhar mein chaand ka aakaar badalta hua kyon lagta hai?
answer: The Moon goes around the Earth; half of it is always lit by the Sun, and from Earth we see different amounts of that lit half on different days.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare the Moon on Purnima and on Amavasya. What do we see, and is the Moon still there on Amavasya?
prompt_hi: Purnima aur Amavasya ke chaand ki tulna karo. Dono din kya dikhta hai, aur kya Amavasya ko chaand wahan hota hai?
answer: Purnima: we see the whole lit face, bright and round. Amavasya: we can't see it; it is still there, but its lit side faces away from us and it is close to the Sun in the sky.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Sometimes you can see the Moon in the morning sky while the Sun is also up. How is that possible if the Moon 'belongs to the night'?
prompt_hi: Kabhi-kabhi subah ke aasmaan mein Sooraj ke saath chaand bhi dikh jaata hai. Agar chaand 'raat ka' hai, toh ye kaise hota hai?
answer: The Moon is above the horizon during part of the day on many days; it shines by reflected sunlight, so it can be seen in daylight when it is up in the sky and bright enough.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Here is Aman's moon diary with four drawings: thin crescent, half-moon, almost full, full. Put them in the order he would see them after Amavasya, and name the last one.
prompt_hi: Ye Aman ki moon diary hai jisme chaar drawings hain: patla chaand, aadha chaand, lagbhag poora, poora gol. Amavasya ke baad jis kram mein dikhenge us kram mein lagao, aur aakhri wale ka naam batao.
answer: thin crescent → half-moon → almost full → full Moon (Purnima)

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'The Moon is a giant bulb that switches itself on at night.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Chaand ek bada sa bulb hai jo raat ko apne aap jal jaata hai.' Galat kya hai?
answer: The Moon makes no light of its own; it shines because sunlight falls on it and bounces to us.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why the Moon looks like a thin slice on some nights and a full circle on others.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki chaand kuch raaton ko patli phaank jaisa aur kuch raaton ko poora gol kyon dikhta hai.
answer: The Sun always lights half of the Moon; as the Moon goes around the Earth over about a month, we see more or less of that lit half, from a thin slice to a full circle; the Moon itself stays round, and it is not the Earth's shadow.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: after Purnima, does the Moon's lit part grow or shrink?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Purnima ke baad chaand ka roshan hissa badhta hai ya ghatta hai?
answer: It shrinks, until Amavasya.

subject: hindi
prompt_en: In the poem, what was the bird's very first home like?
prompt_hi: कविता में चिड़िया का सबसे पहला घर किसके जैसा था?
answer: अंडे जैसा

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Then her home became a nest. What was the nest made of?
prompt_hi: फिर उसका घर घोंसला बना। वह घोंसला किससे बना था?
answer: सूखे तिनकों से

subject: hindi
prompt_en: When the bird says the world is ‘इतना-सा’, does she mean very small or very big?
prompt_hi: चिड़िया कहती है संसार ‘इतना-सा’ है। ‘इतना-सा’ यानी बहुत छोटा या बहुत बड़ा?
answer: बहुत छोटा

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Lines in the poem end with आकार, तैयार and सुकुमार. Which word rhymes with all of them each time?
prompt_hi: कविता की पंक्तियाँ ‘आकार’, ‘तैयार’, ‘सुकुमार’ पर ख़त्म होती हैं। इन सबसे हर बार तुक मिलाने वाला शब्द कौन-सा आता है?
answer: संसार

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Say a new word, not in the poem, that rhymes with संसार.
prompt_hi: ‘संसार’ से तुक मिलाता कोई नया शब्द बोलो, जो कविता में नहीं है।
answer: कोई भी ‘-आर’ वाला शब्द (जैसे — बाज़ार, त्योहार, अनार)

subject: hindi
prompt_en: The branches in the poem were ‘सुकुमार’. What does सुकुमार mean?
prompt_hi: कविता में शाखें ‘सुकुमार’ थीं। ‘सुकुमार’ का मतलब क्या है?
answer: कोमल, नाज़ुक

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Put the bird's homes in order: (क) the sky (ख) the nest (ग) the egg (घ) the branches.
prompt_hi: चिड़िया की दुनिया कैसे बढ़ी? सही क्रम लगाओ — (क) आसमान (ख) घोंसला (ग) अंडा (घ) शाखें।
answer: ग, ख, घ, क (अंडा → घोंसला → शाखें → आसमान)

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Flying far across the sky, what did the bird finally understand?
prompt_hi: आसमान में दूर तक उड़कर चिड़िया को आख़िर में क्या समझ आया?
answer: कि संसार बहुत बड़ा है

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Each time the bird thought the world was tiny, and at last it felt huge. Did the world really change, or did something else change? Why?
prompt_hi: हर बार चिड़िया को संसार छोटा लगा, और आख़िर में बहुत बड़ा। क्या संसार सच में बदला, या कुछ और बदला? क्यों?
answer: संसार वही था; चिड़िया बड़ी होती गई और दूर तक देख पाई, इसलिए उसे संसार बड़ा लगा

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Explain to your little brother or sister how the bird's world changed four times, and what she learned at the end.
prompt_hi: अपने छोटे भाई या बहन को समझाओ — चिड़िया की दुनिया चार बार कैसे बदली, और आख़िर में उसे क्या पता चला?
answer: अंडा → सूखे तिनकों का घोंसला → हरी-भरी कोमल शाखें → खुला आसमान; हर बार लगा संसार इतना-सा है, आख़िर में समझ आया कि संसार बहुत बड़ा है

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Like the bird, your world was small when you were little. What was it then, and what has been added to it now? Tell in two sentences.
prompt_hi: चिड़िया की तरह, जब तुम बहुत छोटे थे तो तुम्हारी दुनिया छोटी थी। तब वह क्या थी, और अब उसमें क्या-क्या जुड़ गया है? दो वाक्यों में बताओ।
answer: दो वाक्य: पहले की छोटी दुनिया और अब की बड़ी दुनिया (जैसे — पहले मेरी दुनिया बस मेरा घर था। अब उसमें स्कूल, दोस्त और पार्क भी हैं।)

subject: hindi
prompt_en: I wrote: ‘चिडिया दूर तक उडी।’ There are two mistakes — catch them both.
prompt_hi: मैंने लिखा — ‘चिडिया दूर तक उडी।’ इसमें दो ग़लतियाँ छिपी हैं, दोनों पकड़ो!
answer: चिड़िया और उड़ी — दोनों में नीचे बिंदु वाला ड़ आएगा

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Three pictures: an egg, a wing, a straw. Say each name. Which name has NO nasal dot (ं)?
prompt_hi: तीन तस्वीरें हैं — अंडा, पंख और तिनका। तीनों के नाम बोलो। किस नाम में बिंदी (ं) नहीं लगती?
answer: तिनका

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Where did the snail live?
prompt_hi: घोंघा कहाँ रहता था?
answer: एक छोटे-से सुंदर बगीचे में

subject: hindi
prompt_en: How long did the snail take to get from one end of the garden to the other?
prompt_hi: बगीचे के एक छोर से दूसरे छोर तक पहुँचने में घोंघे को कितना समय लगता था?
answer: पूरे दो दिन

subject: hindi
prompt_en: How did the snail get out of the garden?
prompt_hi: घोंघा बगीचे से बाहर कैसे निकला?
answer: बगीचे की दीवार के छेद से

subject: hindi
prompt_en: With a rustling sound, the snail felt the whole sky had been covered. What had really happened, and why did it feel like that?
prompt_hi: खड़-खड़ की आवाज़ हुई और घोंघे को लगा कि पूरा आकाश ढँक गया। असल में क्या हुआ था, और उसे ऐसा क्यों लगा?
answer: उसके ऊपर एक सूखा पत्ता गिरा था; घोंघा बहुत छोटा है, इसलिए पत्ता उसे आकाश जितना बड़ा लगा

subject: hindi
prompt_en: To us, the big stone is just a stone. To the snail it looked like something else. What, and why the difference?
prompt_hi: हमें वह बड़ा पत्थर बस एक पत्थर लगता है। घोंघे को वह किसके जैसा लगा, और यह फ़र्क़ क्यों है?
answer: पहाड़ जैसा — क्योंकि घोंघा बहुत छोटा है और उसने इतनी बड़ी चीज़ पहले कभी नहीं देखी थी

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Put in story order what the snail saw: (क) the banyan tree (ख) the big playground (ग) the red ants.
prompt_hi: घोंघे ने बाहर जो देखा, उसे कहानी के क्रम में लगाओ — (क) बड़ का पेड़ (ख) बड़ा मैदान (ग) लाल चींटे।
answer: ख, ग, क (मैदान → चींटे → बड़ का पेड़)

subject: hindi
prompt_en: Outside, the snail said everything in the world moves so fast. Why did he feel that?
prompt_hi: बाहर आकर घोंघे को लगा कि यहाँ हर चीज़ बड़ी फुर्ती से भागती है। उसे ऐसा क्यों लगा?
answer: क्योंकि बगीचे में सब धीरे-धीरे चलता था, और बाहर गिलहरी फुदक रही थी, गेंद लुढ़क रही थी, कुत्ता भाग रहा था

subject: hindi
prompt_en: What is the opposite of धीरे?
prompt_hi: ‘धीरे’ का उल्टा क्या होगा?
answer: तेज़
